pan_head_screw_000035.label: ground-truth-mismatch
pan_head_screw_000035.note: everything but the thread is exact (unthreaded 1492.07 mm3). Our swept V-groove removes 24.07 mm3 (= groove area 0.0924 mm2 x centroid path length, the geometric truth); CadQuery's own sweep solid of the groove has 25.45 mm3 with isFrenet=False (the dataset's setting) and 24.14 with isFrenet=True, the same as ours. The dataset program then cuts that groove from the shank with its outer edge lying exactly ON the shank cylinder (groove vertices at r = 3 = shank radius), and OCCT's cut removes only 10.31 mm3 from a bare shank cylinder (40 percent of its own tool volume: the tangent-touching groove is only partly cut; the dataset part removes 10.08), so the reference is not the geometric groove and cannot be matched without reproducing an OCCT boolean failure.

rect_frame_008694.label: kernel-bug
rect_frame_008694.note: silent wrong fillet around the window: filleting the 12 edges of the back face (outer rectangle, 4-corner window, 4 holes) gives volume 43433.87 / area 28419.0 vs CadQuery 43446.95 / 28324.4 (area +0.33%, validate clean). Per group against CadQuery (same fillet r 1.07, run on the same face edges): outer rectangle alone 43591.530 / 28588.323 and holes alone 43730.228 / 28853.894 are identical to CadQuery, but the four window edges alone are blendFailed at r 0.5, 1.0, 1.07 and 1.5 (CadQuery: 43632.81 / 28668.54), and together with the other groups they remove 13.2 mm3 too much. The window corners are 270 degree material corners (concave vertical edge), where two filleted edges meet.

pan_head_screw_000035.label: ground-truth-mismatch
pan_head_screw_000035.note: the reference STEP is itself non-manifold (one EDGE_CURVE is used by four oriented edges of the thread faces); we import it faithfully (volume, area, bbox, com all match) and validate reports SHELL_NONMANIFOLD for that edge.

j_hook_001383.label: kernel-bug
j_hook_001383.note: STEP import: volume 32302.8365 and area 12218.3437 match the reference, validate is clean, but the body box (mesh-derived) stops at z 102.24 instead of 136.24: the half-torus handle face does not contribute to the box (not tessellated).

propeller_000192.label: kernel-bug
propeller_000192.note: STEP import: VERTEX_OFF_CURVE (3 issues), volume 23814.1 vs 23868.8 (-0.23%), area -0.57%; the reference is the CadQuery union of four ellipse lofts.

OCCT's own booleans of the crossed blades are imprecise: for blade 0 and blade 90 it reports a union of 2792.18 but an intersection of 143.52, and va + vb - union = 145.28, so its two operations disagree by 1.8 mm3; a Monte Carlo of the two solids with OCCT's point classifier (300k points) gives an overlap of 136.3 +- 1.1 mm3, ours is 134.70 (union 2802.77, intersection 134.70, they agree to 1e-7). Each of the four neighbouring pairs is ~9 mm3 too small a union in the reference, which is the 24 mm3 (0.10 percent) and the 12.7 mm2 (0.12 percent) by which ours exceeds it.

torsion_spring_000054.note: the ground-truth coil is an OCC pipe approximation: every sampled point of its two sweep faces lies 0 to +4.2 um outside the ideal screw tube (mean +2.1 um, tests/multi_solid_step.rs torsion_spring_gt_coil_vs_ideal_tube), which inflates the coil volume by 0.12%. Ours is within 3e-5 mm of the ideal tube and equals the closed-form A*2*pi*R*N (N = height/pitch = 11.9977 revolutions): 165057.3. Volume therefore differs from the dataset by 0.11% while the geometry is the more exact one.
